title: Tz-L-M
hookLine: tzelem, image, as in the image of God

cards: Rush hour. A train car packed shoulder to shoulder. A man asleep against the window, mouth open.
A teenager with headphones and a scowl. A woman doing her makeup in her phone's camera. Someone humming, someone crying quietly behind sunglasses.
Nobody looks at anybody. The first chapter of Genesis makes a claim about every one of those faces, in one short word. Tzadi, lamed, mem: Tz-L-M.

teach.h: IN THE IMAGE OF GOD CREATED HE HIM.
teach.b: You met this verse on day twenty-four; today, the word inside it. First: "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him; male and female created He them."
Tzelem, twice, and then a line so nobody misses who's included: male and female. Second, what the word names elsewhere.

teach.h: A TZELEM: A FIGURE THAT STANDS FOR.
teach.b: In other books, tzelem can mean a statue, like the images of Baal that the people of the land break in pieces in the book of Kings. A tzelem stands for someone.
So Genesis takes a word for a carved figure and uses it for a person made of dust and breath. Third, the coins.

teach.h: ONE SEAL, AND NO TWO ALIKE.
teach.b: The Mishnah, in tractate Sanhedrin, says: a human king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all come out alike. God stamped every person with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another.
Fourth, what follows. After the flood, God tells Noah that whoever sheds a person's blood will answer for it, "for in the image of God made He man."

teach.h: HARM A PERSON, STRIKE THE IMAGE.
teach.b: Harm a person, and you've struck at the image. Rabbi Akiva, in Pirkei Avot, adds a softer line: a human is beloved, created in the image, and more beloved still that it was made known to him.
Back to the train car. Genesis doesn't say those faces are nice, or right, or easy to sit next to. It says each one carries the image.

how: Jewish teaching draws on tzelem Elohim, the image of God in every person, when it speaks about human dignity; the Mishnah's teaching about one seal and no two faces alike is studied as part of tractate Sanhedrin.

o: shadow, a darkness that follows each person around
image, as in every person made in the image of God
a seal or stamp, pressed into wax or a coin

s: Genesis says only the man was made in God's image
the verse adds: "male and female created He them."
elsewhere in the Bible, tzelem can mean a statue
the book of Kings uses it for the images of Baal.
in the Mishnah, everyone stamped with God's seal comes out the same
a king's coins come out alike; God's seal makes no two people alike.

games.q: a king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all come out alike. God stamps every person with one seal. what comes out?
o: people who are all the same.
people who are each unlike any other.
games.why: the Mishnah says not one is like another. one image, endless faces.

practice: Bring to mind a face you passed recently without really seeing it: a stranger in a line, a driver, someone you find hard.

Notice one thing about it that no other face has, a crease, a habit, the way they stand: one seal, and no two alike. Stay with that face for a few breaths, and if you pray, hold that person in the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Tz-L-M. Tzadi, lamed, mem: tzelem, image, the word Genesis uses for every human being made in the image of God. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: image; as in tzelem Elohim, the image of God.

carryVoice: Your line: the image. Even the scowler by the window carries it. Rest well.
